claims.text: A rain gauge collects and measures rainfall: it is sunk into open ground so its rim is level with the surface and no splash enters, and each morning the water it holds is poured into a measuring cylinder and read in millimetres.

claims.text: A maximum-minimum thermometer records the day's temperatures: the maximum thermometer marks the highest reading since it was last reset with a small steel index pushed up by the mercury or spirit, and the minimum thermometer, held horizontally or tilted, marks the lowest; both are reset by shaking or with a magnet after reading.

claims.text: A Stevenson screen is a white wooden box with louvred sides standing on legs about one metre above the ground: the white paint reflects sunlight, the louvres let air flow freely while keeping the thermometers in shade, and the legs hold the box above the heat of the ground surface, so the thermometers read the true air temperature.

claims.text: A wet-and-dry bulb thermometer (hygrometer) measures humidity: two matched thermometers stand side by side, one with its bulb wrapped in a damp muslin wick; when the air is dry the water evaporates and cools the wet bulb, so the difference between the two readings shows how humid the air is, and where the two read the same the air is saturated.

claims.text: Wind is measured with two instruments: an anemometer measures wind speed as its cups spin in the wind, and a wind vane shows wind direction, named for the point of the compass the wind blows from.

claims.text: A sunshine recorder measures sunshine with a glass sphere that focuses the sun's rays onto a paper card: the focused light burns a trace along the card, and the length of the burnt trace is read off in hours; a barometer measures air pressure in hectopascals or millibars.

claims.text: Using an instrument is not the same as explaining how it works: using it means saying where it is sited, when and how it is read, and how the reading is recorded and reset - so an answer that describes the mechanism answers a different question from one that describes the use.

claims.text: A diurnal range is the difference between the highest and lowest temperature in one day: maximum reading minus minimum reading, in degrees Celsius; an annual range is the difference between the mean temperature of the hottest and the coolest month.

claims.text: A calculated value uses the readings the question names, with the unit: a range subtracts the lower reading from the higher, a total adds the daily figures, and a mean divides the total by the count of readings - so the answer says which readings were used and carries its unit.
